metadata.note: Pensacola's first rail connection, running north to Montgomery, AL. Pensacola civic leaders (led by Army engineer William Henry Chase) had been planning a railroad into Alabama since the early 1830s -- the Florida Territory chartered the Florida, Alabama and Georgia Rail Road for this purpose in Feb 1834 -- but it took until the Alabama and Florida Railroad Company of Florida (incorporated 1853) for construction to actually happen: the Florida portion broke ground at Pensacola in 1856 and reached Pollard, AL (the junction with the separate Alabama-chartered company building south from Montgomery) in 1861; the Alabama portion reached Montgomery that same May. Through Pensacola-Montgomery passenger service -- a 10-hour trip -- began in May 1861, just as the Civil War was starting. The line passed through several owners afterward: sold to the Pensacola and Louisville Railroad (1868), then the Pensacola Railroad Company (1877), which became a Louisville and Nashville Railroad subsidiary Oct 20 1880. See pensacola_atlantic_railroad.geojson for Pensacola's other rail approach, built eastward toward Jacksonville in the 1880s. Geometry follows real towns along the corridor (Pensacola-Century-Pollard-Brewton-Evergreen-Greenville-Montgomery); the Montgomery-Brewton-Evergreen-Greenville stretch reuses the same real-town waypoints as gulf_breeze_amtrak.geojson's Birmingham-Mobile leg, since both corridors share this trackage before diverging near Brewton/Pollard (one continuing to Mobile, this one turning south into Florida via Century). Pollard's precise coordinates come from its own historical marker; straight-line segments between documented stations, NOT digitized from period track maps.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_and_Florida_Railroad_(1853%E2%80%931869) (Florida portion construction began Pensacola 1856, reached Pollard AL 1861; Alabama portion reached Montgomery May 1861; through Pensacola-Montgomery passenger service, a 10-hour trip, began May 1861)

https://wfrm.org/history/the-pa/ and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola_Railroad (Florida, Alabama and Georgia Rail Road chartered Feb 1834, an earlier unbuilt plan; the line's later ownership chain: Pensacola and Louisville Railroad 1868, Pensacola Railroad Company 1877, L&N subsidiary from Oct 20 1880)

https://encyclopediaofalabama.org/article/pollard/ and https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=130676 (Pollard founded 1861 at the Alabama & Florida / Mobile & Great Northern junction, precise coordinates 31 1.693'N 87 10.345'W; the A&F later rebuilt its junction at nearby Flomaton instead)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact date the line was formally merged into (rather than just controlled by) the L&N; precise frequency for any era, all estimated; whether passenger service continued unbroken through the Civil War given the line opened just as it began.

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
